summary: Azure AD groups-claim missing + stale JWKS cache causing 401/403 for service principals in Private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer reports two related authorization problems after onboarding to Redwood Private: (1) Service principal (client credentials) requests intermittently receive 401 Unauthorized; (2) Many user-service requests succeed but return 403 Forbidden because RBAC role mapping based on Azure AD groups is not being applied. Impact: Several backend jobs and ingestion pipelines using service principals failed to authenticate (intermittent 401s) and web-console actions for 12 engineers were blocked (403) for ~6 hours. Environment: Private control plane in eu-west, version: private-deploy v1.9.2, auth-proxy v0.8.5. Customer SSO: Azure AD (OIDC, v2.0) configured with app registration FinNova-Redwood. Steps to reproduce: 1) Use client credentials flow to request access token from azure v2 endpoint for FinNova-Redwood app. 2) Call Redwood private API endpoint /v1/models with Authorization: Bearer <token>. 3) Observe 401 logs in auth-proxy or 403 when calling console endpoints that require group-based role. Expected: Stable 200s for machine-to-machine tokens and RBAC enforcement that maps Azure groups to Redwood roles. Actual: Intermittent 401 after Azure AD key rotation and consistent 403 for tokens lacking "groups" claim. Error excerpts: - auth-proxy.log: "jwt validation failed: key id mismatch (kid: Wq9a2...)" - rbac.log: "role mapping: no groups claim found, default deny" Related customer notes: Customer enabled 'group assignments' for users but did not set groupMembershipClaims in app manifest; they also use an automation account (service principal) which, by design, doesn't receive groups in client credentials flow unless configured.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 09:20 - Initial triage: Reproduced 401s from FinNova IP range. Observed repeated jwt verification failures with KID mismatch in auth-proxy. Correlated with Azure AD key rollover event (MS telemetry indicates key rotation at 2026-03-12T08:55Z).

2026-03-12 11:05 - Checked auth-proxy JWKS cache TTL: config set to 24h (default). Hypothesis: auth-proxy did not refresh JWKS quickly after rotation, causing stale keys to be used and intermittent 401s until cache expired or manual reload done.

2026-03-12 13:40 - Investigated 403s: tokens from browser-based interactive users sometimes lacked "groups" claim. Confirmed app registration FinNova-Redwood did not have 'groupMembershipClaims' set. Azure AAD returns groups in tokens only if configured and for user flows; client credentials flows do not receive groups by default.

2026-03-12 14:10 - Tested workaround: Forced auth-proxy JWKS refresh by POST /internal/refresh-jwks -> immediate drop in 401s for subsequent requests. For group claim issue, issued interactive login token after updating app manifest locally and observed groups claim present and RBAC mapping applied.

2026-03-13 09:00 - SRE running capture: added extra logging for token source (client_credentials vs authorization_code) and added metrics to track tokens without groups claim vs with groups claim. Linked logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/fin-nova/auth/2026-03-12

2026-03-13 10:30 - Confirmed two root causes: (A) stale JWKS cache + rotation -> 401s; (B) Azure AD configuration + OIDC client-credentials semantics -> missing 'groups' claim causing 403 when role mapping depends on groups.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:45 - Customer (FinNova SRE): 'We started seeing automation failures around 09:00 UTC. Tokens validated yesterday but now some calls return 401. Any quick mitigation?'

2026-03-12 10:00 - Support (Maya Patel): 'Thanks. We're looking into it. Can you share a failing request ID and whether these are machine-to-machine or user tokens? Also please confirm the azure app registration name.'
2026-03-12 10:20 - Customer: 'Request IDs: req-9f3a2b / req-9f3a8c. These are CI jobs using the service principal (client credentials). App registration is FinNova-Redwood-prod.'

2026-03-12 11:30 - Support (Diego Ramos): 'We've triggered a JWKS refresh on your private control plane; can you re-run one job and share results? Also, please do not rotate the app keys until we confirm stabilization.'
2026-03-12 11:45 - Customer: 'After JWKS refresh, one job succeeded but another still returned 401. We see intermittent success.'

2026-03-12 14:25 - Support (Diego Ramos): 'We're continuing to investigate. Two parallel items: we'll deploy a short-lived patch to reduce JWKS cache TTL to 5 minutes in the auth-proxy for your tenant and provide guidance for enabling groups in Azure AD app manifest.'

2026-03-13 15:02 - Customer: 'Updated our app manifest to set groupMembershipClaims = "All" and reissued interactive tokens; console access restored for engineers but CI jobs still show 401 occasionally.'

2026-03-14 08:50 - Support (Diego Ramos): 'Patch deployed to your auth-proxy to auto-refresh JWKS on 401 and set a short TTL. We've validated a 72h window: no 401s observed for 24h of sampling. We'll keep monitoring and provide a postmortem and KB.'
resolution: Immediate remediation: (1) Deployed auth-proxy patch to FinNova tenant: reduce JWKS cache TTL from 24h -> 5m and add auto-refresh-on-401 logic. (2) Provided step-by-step guidance to FinNova: set 'groupMembershipClaims' to 'All' in Azure AD app manifest for interactive user tokens and create a service-to-service role mapping for client credentials (since group claims are not included by default for app-only tokens). Final state: Interactive user RBAC restored after manifest change; service principal flows stabilized after JWKS patch and guidance to use certificate-based auth with matching app config. Follow-ups: create KB article documenting Azure AD app manifest requirements for group-based RBAC (SUP-KB-148), add monitoring alert for sudden JWKS KID mismatches, and add automated JWKS refresh in the global auth-proxy config. Customer acceptance: FinNova SRE confirmed pipelines and console access recovered and will monitor for 48h.
